newsitem.title: UK: London gold stays dull, awaits next move.
newsitem.headline: London gold stays dull, awaits next move.

text.p: The gold market held quiet and fairly steady around the $380 per ounce level on Monday afternoon but dealers said expectations were still for a fall.
"It is very dull indeed. There is a lot of bearish sentiment around and there may be another splash to come," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $380.10 after $379.60 this morning and a Friday close of $380.20/$380.70.
At the fixing the Comex December futures were $0.20 down at $382.40 after forecasts of an unchanged to $0.50 lower opening.
Dealers said there was very little business being done.
Technically, gold's 10-day moving average was flattening out slightly, while the 30-day indicator proceeded in a steady downward slope.
The RSI was creeping higher at 39, although the market was still seen quite short.
"It's still oversold and it won't be suprising if there's some sort of recovery," a European analyst said. "But it's probably more likely to test the lower end of the range."
A London-based dealer commented, "When everybody is looking the one way it usually goes the other, so maybe you should buy."
He added that producers could be waiting for a bounce.
"They may have held off and gearing up to sell into a rally," he said, adding that this would make a limited upside, at least in the short term.
"A lot of the shorts have got puts in place which lets them buy when they think (the price) is down," he said.
But dealers and analyst were unanimous that the funds held the key to gold's next move. "It's down to the funds unless something new comes along," one dealer said.
Lease rates were slightly easier than Friday and back around levels seen at the beginning of last week, although still well above mid-September levels.
Some dealers said most of the dynamic behind the moves in lease rates was fund short covering rather than producer or rumoured central bank selling.

"Most of the borrowing we saw recently was for a month. The lending that has come into the market is mainly for one or two weeks, suggesting the funds are lending back their unused cover," a dealer said.
The other metals were very quiet. Silver was four cents lower at $4.87/$4.89, platinum was 80 cents off at $383.10/$384.10 and palladium down $1.00 at $119.00/$120.00.
